RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

An all-women panel chose a woman over another woman. The panel's composition can't plausibly explain why you lost to a same-sex candidate, and raising it would read as a complaint that women shouldn't judge hiring — which damages your credibility on the point that actually matters.

What matters is substantive: they preferred eight years plus "strong experience of digital media" over your fifteen years and five as deputy. That's either a genuine, defensible priority or a thin rationalisation of a decision already made. You can't tell which until you see the reasons.

So press the real failure: a written explanation is two weeks overdue. Send a dated follow-up, copy HR, cite any internal policy on feedback timelines, and ask for the scoring against the published criteria.
